item.title: Screen/Society--"Samba Traoré" (Idrissa Ouédraogo, 1992) | new 4K restoration — Tue Sep 22, 7:00 PM — Rubenstein Arts Center
item.description:
Film Screening:
"Samba Traoré" (Idrissa Ouédraogo, 1992, 85 min, Burkina Faso/France/Switzerland; in Mooré, Dyula, and French with English subtitles, DCP)
The only surviving accomplice of a gas station robbery gone bad, Samba Traoré flees the scene of the crime with a suitcase full of cash for his native village in rural Burkina Faso. There he attempts to make a fresh start while hiding how he came by his new fortune from those around him. Despite marrying the beautiful Saratou, earning the affection of her ten-year-old son, and opening a bar with his childhood friend, Samba's newfound happiness is put to the test as he struggles to cope with the moral crisis of his crimes.
Shortly after winning the Grand Prix at Cannes with "The Law" ["Tilaï"] in 1990, Burkinabe writer-director Idrissa Ouédraogo followed up that dazzling work with the remarkable "Samba Traoré" (1992), a gripping noir film revolving around the conflicts between city and rural life as well as modernity and tradition

item.title: Duke Arts Presents: Mo Amer — Tue Sep 22, 7:30 PM — Page Auditorium
item.description:
Trailblazing comedian Mo Amer brings his sharp, deeply-personal stand-up to Durham to help kick off the Duke Arts Presents season. Known for his acclaimed series MO and three stand-up specials on Netflix, Amer has built a global following with comedy that blends personal storytelling, cultural insight, and fearless humor.
Drawing from his experiences as a Palestinian-American, immigrant, husband, and father, Amer's comedy moves effortlessly between the personal and political with warmth and candor. His series MO earned a rare 100% critics score on Rotten Tomatoes and a Peabody Award, while his standup has taken him to stages in more than 40 countries. Expect a night of smart, surprising, and deeply human comedy in this can't-miss event.
Source: Duke University

item.title: Duke Campus Farm Community Work Day — Wed Sep 23, 9:00 AM — Duke Campus Farm
item.description:
ome join us in the fields to lose track of time, be outdoors, practice embodied work, and experience profound community with plants, soil, and humans! Our students, volunteers, and staff consistently say that their most memorable memories at DCF are the conversations they shared over a wheelbarrow of mulch or while tackling weeds in a bed of carrots together. item.title: Raising Accountability while Managing a Hybrid Team — Wed Sep 23, 9:00 AM — None
item.description:
For employees of Duke University and DUHS. Continuing Education Credits (CEUs): 0.4
When supervising a hybrid team of employees, you worry whether or not you are getting as much from their job performance as employees who remain physically on the Duke premises. On the other hand, you and your entire team may be working off site full time. Building a bonded, high functioning, and collaborative team requires a combination of knowledge and skills, and clear communication strategies.
Fortunately, technology has come a long way in allowing your team(s) to tap into a multitude of available resources at Duke. This course will teach you the best ways to motivate yourself and your team to connect, inspire and collaborate with one another.
Source: Duke University

item.title: Migrating Monarchs — Wed Sep 23, 10:00 AM — Prairie Ridge
item.description:
All programs at Prairie Ridge currently require registration. Register Join us for a front-row seat to one of nature’s most incredible journeys, the Monarch butterfly migration! We’ll start this family friendly program in our Nature Neighborhood Garden to explore the habitats we steward here at Prairie Ridge and see how these spaces fuel Monarchs along their trek south. Then, we’ll head into the prairie to spot as many butterflies as we can! If we’re lucky, we might even catch and release a live Monarch butterfly. We will learn about the Monarch Larvae Monitoring Project and Monarch Watch collaborative science projects along the way.
Source: NC Museum of Natural Sciences

item.title: iNaturalist Together After Dark — Fri Sep 25, 7:00 PM — Prairie Ridge
item.description:
All programs at Prairie Ridge currently require registration. Register Join fellow iNaturalist users for an evening at Prairie Ridge as we investigate the wildlife that is active at night. We’ll sweep net for insects, take a short walk to the pond to listen for frogs and birds, and have light stations to attract moths and other nocturnal insects. Bring a flashlight and a smartphone or camera so you can photograph and document what you see. This program includes a brief introduction to iNaturalist, including a few advanced features you may not know about before we head out to the frog and insect stations. Show up with iNaturalist already installed on your phone and a flashlight for the best experience!
Source: NC Museum of Natural Sciences

item.title: Nature Play Day at NCMA — Mon Sep 28, 10:00 AM — North Carolina Museum of Art
item.description:

We will be stocking part of the outdoor park with extra special materials and supplies to encourage nature exploration and outdoor play! A Prairie Ridge play facilitator will be present to help you play your way. item.title: Food Prep Workshop — Mon Sep 28, 6:00 PM — Nature Research Center
item.description:
Come help the Museum’s Green Team celebrate Food Waste Prevention Week with a workshop on food prep! Take the stress out of mealtime! Learn simple, practical ways to plan your meals, organize your grocery shopping, and prep ahead—so you can spend less time wondering “What’s for dinner?” and more time enjoying meals with the people you love. Whether you’re feeding a family or just trying to make your week run smoother, you’ll leave with tools and strategies you can actually use. Participants will leave with their own silicone storage cube, that they will prep during the session! Workshop is free but registration is required. REGISTER HERE
Source: NC Museum of Natural Sciences

In this technique/creative dance class, we will do so in a healthy, FUN way. We will warm the body, moving in a way that encourages each dancer to better honor and understand their unique physicality. Next, dancers will explore different ways to generate movement phrases. item.title: Teen Science Café: Unwinding Spiral Galaxies — Fri Oct 2, 6:00 PM — Downtown Raleigh
item.description:
The winding arms of spiral galaxies are one of their most obvious features. By measuring how tightly the arms are wrapped, we can reveal clues about other components that are much harder to observe, such as dark matter content and central black hole mass. We aim to partner volunteers with AI in order to identify individual spiral arms in tens of thousands of galaxies, measure how tightly each arm is wound, and use those measurements to estimate these elusive properties. Doing so will help us better understand how galaxies similar to our own Milky Way form and evolve.
About the Presenter Dr. Patrick Treuthardt is the Assistant Head of the Astronomy & Astrophysics Research Lab at the North Carolina Museum of Natural Sciences and a Research Affiliate in the Department of Computing Sciences at Coastal Carolina University. item.title: "The Problem of Personhood:" Book talk & discussion with author Lisa Siraganian — Tue Sep 22, 5:30 PM — Smith Warehouse
item.description:
Reception with light refreshments starts at 5:15pm. Siraganian's talk starts at 5:30pm. Copies of the book will be sold at the event.
SHOULD NONHUMANS HAVE RIGHTS IN LAW AND POLITICS?
Over the last twenty-five years, the concept of per-sonhood has become central to many contentious debates. Corporations have won free speech protections, as if they were individuals. The right to life or freedom has been claimed on behalf of fetuses, trees, and elephants. The fund of human rights is spilling over into the nonhuman.
The Problem of Personhood reveals the unsettling consequences of granting rights to imagined persons, such as Sophia the robot citizen or New Zealand's Whanganui River. Synthesizing the political and phil­osophical debates on personhood and drawing on a varied cast of thinkers that includes Simone Weil, Hannah Arendt, and Dr. Seuss, Lisa Siraganian un­covers the disturbing impact of this contemporary development.
